overview: This lab kept two directory forests separate while allowing the designated domains to authenticate across an external trust. I prepared name resolution first, then configured the trust and a test share.

steps.title: Prepare DC03 networking
steps.description: I configured the third controller VM with its static lab address and the network settings needed for the new directory environment.

steps.title: Install AD DS and create the partner forest
steps.description: I installed AD DS and selected Add a new forest on DC03 rather than adding it as a replica of the existing domain.

steps.title: Configure and check the forwarder on DC01
steps.description: I added a conditional forwarder for the partner domain on DC01 and checked the target DNS server in its properties.

steps.title: Configure and check the reciprocal forwarder
steps.description: I added the reverse conditional forwarder on DC03 so each namespace could direct partner-domain DNS queries to the other controller.

steps.title: Open the domain trust configuration
steps.description: I inspected the primary domain’s Trusts tab and launched the New Trust wizard.

steps.title: Specify the partner domain
steps.description: I entered the second domain’s name, using the DNS configuration prepared in the preceding steps to locate it.

steps.title: Select an external trust
steps.description: I chose External trust, which connects the specified domains without making the trust transitive to other domains.

steps.title: Select the two-way direction
steps.description: I configured the trust in both directions so each designated domain could accept authentication from the other.

steps.title: Create both sides of the trust
steps.description: I selected Both this domain and the specified domain and supplied authorized administrative authentication to create both trust objects. Those sign-in values are not retained in the public images.

steps.title: Set the lab authentication scope
steps.description: I selected Domain-wide authentication for both sides as required by the exercise. Resource permissions still determine what an authenticated principal can access.

steps.title: Confirm outgoing and incoming trust paths
steps.description: I completed the wizard and used its outgoing and incoming confirmation steps to check the configured relationship.

steps.title: Inspect both domains’ trust lists
steps.description: I checked the primary and partner Trusts tabs. Each lists an external trust in both directions with non-transitive behavior.

steps.title: Create the dedicated test folder
steps.description: I created the cross-domain test folder on DC01 to provide a specific resource for the authentication and permission exercise.

steps.title: Enable advanced sharing
steps.description: I opened Advanced Sharing and enabled the test share.

steps.title: Resolve the partner-domain principal
steps.description: I changed the object-selection location to the partner domain and used Check Names to resolve the authorized test principal across the trust.

steps.title: Apply the lab share permissions
steps.description: I gave the resolved partner principal the permissions required by the test. The exercise uses an administrator and Full Control, rather than demonstrating a minimal operational grant.

steps.title: Connect from the partner domain
steps.description: I used a UNC path from DC03 to reach DC01 and checked the visible shared resource. The retained image shows the server’s share listing.

steps.title: Record the resource-access test
steps.description: My notes describe opening the shared folder and creating a test file. I retain this as a documented test because the supplied final screenshot shows share discovery rather than that file operation.

checks.title: Reciprocal DNS and trust configuration
checks.description: The captures show the forwarders and both domains’ external trust lists.

checks.title: Cross-domain share discovery
checks.description: The partner-domain session can list the resource shared by DC01.

checks.title: Folder and file operation
checks.description: The report describes opening the share and creating a file; the retained image does not independently show file creation.

lessons: Cross-domain authentication depends on being able to resolve the partner namespace.
A two-way trust is still constrained by its type and the resource permissions.
Trust establishes an authentication path; it does not automatically grant access to every shared folder.
Selective authentication and narrower non-administrative grants should be considered for a real cross-organization requirement.
scope: Domain-wide authentication and administrator Full Control were training choices. The captured evidence establishes trust configuration and share discovery, while the file-creation result remains supported by the written notes.
